newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo returns Rwandan helicopters.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo returns Rwandan helicopters.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of the Congo on Thursday handed back to Rwanda three helicopters taken into the ex-Zaire by former Rwandan government troops who lost a civil war in 1994.
The handover ceremony took place at Kinshasa's Ndjili international airport as Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu was closing a two-day working visit to Kinshasa.

Bizimungu and Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni ended summit talks with Congo President Laurent Kabila on Wednesday. Rwanda and Uganda backed Kabila in his seven-month-long guerrilla campaign that toppled veteran Zairean dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.

"The government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has given back to the government of Rwanda three helicopters taken away into the Congolese territory in July 1994 by fleeing forces of the former Rwandan army," Kabila's Foreign Minister, Bizima Karaha, told reporters before the handover ceremony.

"The Congolese government has reiterated its firm willingness to carry on investigations in order to retrieve military equipment and other belongings of Rwanda," Bizima said, reading from a statement.
Kabila's government had received a list of such property from Rwanda, he added.
Relations between Rwanda and the former Zaire soured in 1994 after the victory of Tutsi-led Patriotic Front rebels over the Hutu-dominated army of former president Juvenal Habyarimana.

Habyarimana was a Mobutu ally. The Hutu president's death in an unexplained plane crash triggered a massacre of about 800,000 minority Tutsis by Hutus, but the Tutsis went on to win the war, sending Hutus fleeing into then-Zaire.
Hundreds of Habyarimana's armed soldiers were among the 1.5 million Rwandan Hutus who crossed the border in mid-1994.
The Kabila rebels who toppled Mobutu were dominated by ethnic Tutsis and backed by Rwandan Tutsi soldiers, many of whom are still in the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Rwanda, Uganda, Burundi and Angola are widely believed to have assisted Kabila militarily.
The Rwandan president left Kinshasa on Thursday for Kigali via the southern Congolese town of Lubumbashi.
